![A page from a 1979 internal IBM training manual. Image via [Simon Willison](https://simonwillison.net/2025/Feb/3/a-computer-can-never-be-held-accountable/).](cover.jpg){fig-align="center"}

[The Register](https://www.theregister.com/ai-and-ml/2026/06/18/estonia-intends-to-recognize-ai-agents-with-digital-ids/) reports that Estonia plans to give AI agents their own digital identities, so an agent acting for a person can be verified and audited. The primary source is a [statement from the Estonian Government Office](https://www.valitsus.ee/en/news/prime-minister-michal-estonia-become-first-country-create-digital-identities-ai-agents): at the second meeting of the [Eesti.ai](http://eesti.ai) advisory board on 17 June 2026, the board agreed to move forward with digital identities for AI agents, which it calls an "AI ID." Prime Minister [Kristen Michal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristen_Michal) put the goal in terms of one question:

> In the future, AI will increasingly carry out digital tasks on our behalf, compiling reports, preparing declarations or interacting with information systems. To that end, it must be clear who is acting on whose behalf with what rights, and who is ultimately responsible.

What the [proposal](https://www.valitsus.ee/en/news/prime-minister-michal-estonia-become-first-country-create-digital-identities-ai-agents) says:

- **Scoped, controllable authority.** An agent acting for a person or company is given limited and controllable powers, instead of the person granting an AI assistant access to all of their rights, services, and data.
- **Per-action permissioning.** The statement is concrete about granularity: it must be possible to specify whether an agent may only view data, prepare a document, draw up a payment, or act solely within a set financial limit.
- **Built on the existing e-state.** The government positions the AI ID as the next layer on the trust infrastructure that already runs the country: a national digital identity, the X-Road data-exchange layer, and legally binding digital signatures.
- **A commitment, with the mechanics still open.** This is an agreement to proceed, reached at an advisory-board meeting. The authorization and delegation mechanics are not defined, and the "first country in the world" claim is conditional on acting "quickly, and smartly."

The Register places the move in a wider scramble over who answers for an agent's actions. Argentina's president [Javier Milei](https://www.ft.com/content/f93022fe-43f7-437d-abd8-06c457c0a43c) has endorsed "non-human corporations" run by software with limited liability. In commerce, [Target's terms](https://www.target.com/c/terms-conditions/-/N-4sr7l) now treat actions by an agent you authorized as transactions you made, while [American Express](https://www.americanexpress.com/en-us/newsroom/articles/innovation/american-express-debuts-agentic-commerce-experiences--ace--devel.html) goes the other way and promises to cover customers when an authorized agent makes a purchase in error. The piece also revives the line from [IBM's 1979 training manual](https://www.ibm.com/think/insights/ai-decision-making-where-do-businesses-draw-the-line), that a computer can never be held accountable and so must never make a management decision, and notes that courts are filling the gap anyway, holding [Air Canada](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/air-canada-chatbot-lawsuit-1.7116416) liable for bad chatbot advice.

## My Notes

- **A digital ID is really about who to blame.** A software agent can't be punished the way a person can, as [Mark Riedl and Deven Desai](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.08544) point out: you can fine or jail a human, not a piece of software. So an AI ID doesn't make the agent answerable. It records who authorized the agent and how much it was allowed to do, so there is finally a clear human to hold responsible when something goes wrong. The commerce terms above are early, ad hoc stabs at the same problem. A national identity layer would settle it the same way every time.

- **Estonia can be first because the hard part is already built.** The AI ID is an increment on e-Estonia's [digital identity](https://e-estonia.com/solutions/estonian-e-identity/), [X-Road data exchange](https://e-estonia.com/solutions/interoperability-services/x-road/), and digital signatures, not a greenfield project. The same fact makes the "first country" claim credible and the approach hard to copy elsewhere: a state without an e-government foundation would have to stand up the identity layer before it could scope an agent's powers at all.
